request.instructions:
You design a complete robot processing method and its cooperation with Jev.
Submit one submit_method call containing explanation, source, interface, and
jev_protocol. All fields and source must be English ASCII. This is a complete
executable method, with observation processing, parameters, bounded feedback
loops, Jev input questions/choices, output interpretation, and recovery logic.
Define main(api); return a JSON-compatible result with completion_proposed and
evidence. The task is runtime data; there is no task recipe or stored trajectory.
Keep the complete source concise, preferably at most 180 lines. Use the minimum
sufficient obtainable evidence for each gate. Repeated descriptions and redundant
checks increase generation and review cost without creating new measurements.
Design the observation dependencies before writing the phase logic. In interface,
list each important gate, its minimal required state components, obtainable
measurement witnesses, retained invariants, and executable occlusion fallback.
Implement those distinctions in source. Do not call an all-purpose full-object
registration routine unconditionally at every phase. A gate needs the components
that its next action actually uses, not every component of a global shape pose.
Landmarks chosen before an intervention can become hidden by the hand; the
ordinary path must still have an attainable local witness or a justified bounded
trial with an independent effect check. A change of camera view is not by itself
evidence of object motion. Retain a stated short-horizon world-geometry prior
only while current partial observations and possible physical interactions remain
consistent with it, with uncertainty and explicit invalidation conditions.
Acquiring a new identified rigid patch for a prospective motion test must not
require first registering that patch to every old shape landmark. Its local
motion reference and a later full-envelope pose have different evidence needs.
This is a bounded simulator episode. Construct an operational method with
observable checks and bounded trials; a full exact reconstruction or certified
collision-free scene model is not required or provided. Use api.drive for ordinary
bounded pose-feedback loops when suitable, and api.control for custom updates.
Reuse geo.rotation, geo.pad_position, geo.plane, geo.circle_xy,
geo.transform and geo.attachment_error where applicable instead of reimplementing
their internals. These are pure mathematical operations, not a task solution.
Contact can occlude an object's perimeter. Where appropriate, initialize a
textured visible patch and use the supplied RGB-D rigid tracker, with its inlier
and uncertainty checks, to observe motion. Do not require every perimeter corner
to remain visible for every local action. Compare observed patch/object motion
with actual hand motion to test retention; a track alone is not grasp evidence.
Tracking is fallible. Include an executable recovery for unknown registration:
request current identifiable corresponding landmarks or another usable patch,
retain their semantic reference definitions, and compare independently observed
motion with the saved reference and robot motion. State uncertainty and reject
ambiguous correspondence. Do not fabricate a transform, assume rigid attachment,
or make an optional tracker the sole gate when another obtainable measurement
can resolve the same question. Stop when neither evidence nor a justified
observation-producing action is available.
Distinguish essential evidence from optional certification unavailable through
this API. When a bounded observation-producing action is justified by current
evidence, use it to resolve uncertainty; do not build circular preconditions
that require the result of an action before allowing that action to begin.
Do not make complete visibility of a later motion corridor a hidden prerequisite
when the API provides no such certificate. Separate observed external obstruction,
unobserved space, and occlusion by the robot or held item. Ask review questions
with explicit meanings for those outcomes rather than an ambiguous clear flag.
Use justified local evidence and bounded progress or a view-changing action;
unknown is not proof of clearance, and self-occlusion alone is not an observed
external obstacle. If no justified local action exists, report the exact gap.

Available Python: np (NumPy), math, geo, ordinary functions and finite for loops.
No imports, class definitions, global/nonlocal statements, while loops, files,
networking, private attributes, dynamic execution,
or simulator access. Resolve every helper. Robot and physical state persist if
your method is repaired; edits and exceptions do not undo motion.
Use bounded episode checkpoints for essential reference measurements and phase
evidence that a repair needs. A checkpoint is historical data with provenance,
not a current sensor value. Revalidate affected dependencies after motion; do
not discard a still-valid measured invariant solely because Python restarted.
New episodes have empty checkpoint memory and must acquire their own evidence.
Useful tracker handles also persist within the same physical episode. Checkpoint
their reference provenance and surface identity; reuse a relevant saved reference
with a fresh track_update after a repair instead of needlessly discarding it.
A historical reference is not a current detection, and unknown still needs recovery.

The supplied manual is the exact API contract. Use only its operations and
schema. Before submission, audit every helper return-key access and every API
argument against that manual, including paths in recovery branches. A descriptive
concept name is not a field alias. Check returned measurement membership and measurement_errors; a requested
pixel or region can fail measurement and is then absent. Handle that locally
before using its geometry. You may process current visible point clouds with NumPy, choose visual
measurement regions, define scalar features and conditional procedures, and
design Jev questions. No force sensing, segmentation IDs, object truth, task
files, reward predicates, or collision planner is available. Do not invent them.
New or repaired methods must supply fields in every api.review call. Declare
only the parameters needed by that call, with exact
types or enum literals, and ask for those same names and meanings. Use the
documented structured fields interface instead of relying on untyped free JSON.
Keep schemas concise and reuse descriptors. Include unknown/null when needed;
schema adherence never establishes that an observation is true.

Geometry must be based on current RGB-D and calibration. A surface point is not
an object center or hidden underside. Use multiple measured visible surfaces or
regions when extent or placement geometry matters. Identify relevant pixels from
images; calculate world geometry in code. Account for the actual fingerpad
offset and gripper opening axis in the supplied robot geometry. Explicitly
distinguish end-effector frame and pad_center. Preserve orientation unless a
justified change is needed. Do not infer finger clearance or contact from a pose
target alone. Unknown geometry requires another view or a declared limitation.

All physical actions go through api.control, which calls real Jev. Define its
questions and their criteria yourself, using exactly the documented choice keys.
Compute numerical magnitudes, tolerances, coordinate transforms and features in
code. Explain in jev_protocol which measured/derived fields are sent, what each
choice means, and how the runtime maps choices to commands. Use api.choose for
additional evidence-based local branch decisions if useful. Jev is a finite
choice model, not a Python interpreter, metric calculator, or undeclared sensor.
Give it clear semantic direction labels derived from current residuals, rather
than requiring arithmetic. Follow the documented quaternion and error signs.

A complete method should reach and assess the final goal, with bounded recovery.
Observe actual outcomes at contact transitions and after release. Freshness and
uncertainty matter: a commanded closure, reached pose, elapsed steps, or intended
lift does not prove retention. Review images to verify object effects when the
program lacks sufficient evidence; api.review is a real GPT call, not a free
detector. Use its new points/regions to refresh moving object references.
Do not keep a stale object point after motion. Avoid repeated reviews of an
unchanged scene without asking a concrete resolvable question.

Local motion tracking, object retention, stable placement, and full task success
are different claims. After release, obtain a new view and assess the actual
object relation and stability. Your completion proposal is not official success.
The native evaluator is isolated and will score the final physical state.
Never inspect or reconstruct its hidden predicates. Respect control and model
budgets; reserve resources for verification and recovery. Complete programs must
handle api.control returning reached, moved, or stalled, and stop or recover on
explicit failures. Do not repeatedly push a stalled contact or reopen a held
object during transfer. Report unresolved limitations truthfully.


Generic development lessons, bounded by recorded development evidence:

- Recovery must be reachable from every relevant measurement call site, not
  just the first use of a helper. An exception or require inside a shared
  observer can bypass a caller's intended alternatives. Handle inconclusive
  measurements at the helper boundary or explicitly at all its callers, with
  finite retries, distinct informative measurements or supported observation
  actions, and preservation of acknowledged physical state. Distinguish this
  outcome from an observed contradiction, actual loss, exhausted resources and
  a programming error; do not catch all failures and silently continue.
  Before submission, follow each important unknown-result path through the
  actual source to its recovery or justified terminal limitation, including
  uses after later interventions. A recovery described only in interface text
  or around an earlier call is not implemented for those later calls.
- Derive measurement adequacy from the next predicate, not an unrelated fixed
  ceiling on one global pose-error scalar. Retain componentwise bounds or a
  bounded set of physically consistent hypotheses when different components
  have different observability. Propagate those dependencies into the actual
  effect margin. Large uncertainty in an unused direction need not make that
  margin inconclusive. If it is inconclusive, seek relevant new information or
  a supported bounded alternative; raising a quality threshold alone creates
  neither a measurement nor evidence that the action will work.
- A failed conservative proxy is not an observed physical impossibility. For
  an effect margin g(theta, x), distinguish nominal feasibility, robust
  feasibility over a stated uncertainty set, and an observed failed trial.
  First search a bounded, geometry-derived set of action parameters theta for
  useful slack; do not treat the first chosen pose or fixed margin as the only
  method. If a conservative bound fails while nominal feasibility remains,
  reduce the relevant uncertainty with a different measurement, test another
  justified configuration, or perform a bounded simulator trial with an
  independent effect check and an executable recovery. Do not relabel that
  uncertainty as proven clearance, or declare the task impossible from a small
  negative proxy slack. An assumed multi-sigma multiplier on a heuristic error
  is not a calibrated guarantee. Track shared/correlated error dependencies so
  the same uncertainty is not charged repeatedly as independent error.
  Each important gate needs separate pass, observed-failure and inconclusive
  behavior in the complete program; returning incomplete at the first
  inconclusive proxy is not recovery. Stop when no supported bounded action or
  informative measurement remains, or the declared trial budget is exhausted.
- Factor the estimated state by the next predicate. If a gate is g(x_S),
  unobservability of unrelated components x_not_S does not establish that g is
  false. Identify the minimal current witness for x_S and explicitly retain or
  invalidate its historical dependencies. Do not make every local action depend
  on a fresh global object transform. Relative surface/effector alignment,
  a support relation, differential motion, and a full transported envelope can
  require different measurements. A returned null for an old mark is not a
  measurement that the body moved. A prior remains a hypothesis, not a detection;
  check current partial evidence and relevant possible interactions before use.
- Initial named landmarks are not a permanent sensor specification. When they
  become hidden, identify an obtainable rigid surface on the same body and form
  a current local reference for the next differential test. Initializing that
  reference does not require a full old-shape registration. Independently measure
  patch/body motion and hand motion after the intervention. If later envelope
  reasoning needs a patch-to-shape relation, establish that relation from then
  obtainable geometry or explicitly retain its uncertainty; do not fabricate it.
  A fallback that simply requests the same hidden marks is not executable recovery.
- Separate a currently justified observation action from a later unobserved
  action. Assess each at its actual scope. Visible partial surfaces can support
  an explicit local geometric model when identity, model assumptions, residuals
  and uncertainty are checked. A model is not a collision certificate. Neither
  missing global visibility nor robot self-occlusion is an observed external
  obstacle; an observed obstruction still forbids the rejected local action.
- Keep persistent state bounded by construction. Save essential reference
  geometry, handles, acknowledgments and phase dependencies; keep diagnostic
  histories as a bounded window outside nested copies of old state. Split
  independent numeric structures within the documented key/value/total limits.
  Audit the worst branch, not just initialization, before calling checkpoint.
- Make geometric gates and numerical control compatible. Derive each local
  stopping tolerance from the measured effect margin and uncertainty. If a
  correction is smaller than a routine's early-return deadband while the effect
  predicate is still false, repeating that routine unchanged cannot fix it.
  Use a justified finer correction or an explicitly supported bounded trial,
  then remeasure the effect. Feature spread is an observability quantity relative
  to residuals and noise, not a universal absolute object-size threshold. Keep
  heuristic uncertainty distinct from calibrated statistical confidence.

- Reference continuity is part of the runtime contract. A source repair does not
  reset the physical episode or its saved patch references. Store useful handles
  and their surface identity in checkpoints. A fresh update must still establish
  current quality; persistence does not certify object identity or attachment.
- For positive overlap m between a translated interval [a+t,b+t] and [c,d],
  feasibility is exactly c+m-b <= t <= d-m-a, provided
  0 < m <= min(b-a,d-c). A finite contact band can overlap a side even if its
  center or its entire band is not contained in that side. Intersect the relevant
  measured overlap and support-clearance constraints in a consistent frame.
  This mathematical identity is not evidence that physical contact occurred.
- A prospective motion test can start from a newly measured, identified patch.
  Its reference gauge need not equal an older full-shape gauge. Compare the
  independently observed patch motion with measured hand motion; do not substitute
  hand motion for an object measurement. Reconstruct a global shape pose only
  when a later action actually needs it. A safe observation-producing action
  still needs phase-local justification, not proof of an unavailable later state.
- With a known rigid planar shape, a measured face plane and an identifiable
  edge direction constrain orientation. An independent physical fiducial can
  resolve translation and finite edge-identity hypotheses. Use visible geometry,
  validate residuals and reject contradicted hypotheses; do not invent hidden corners
  or require an entire old landmark set when sufficient independent evidence exists.
- Separate same-body identity from the correspondence of named marks or indexed
  vertices. A current surface can belong unambiguously to the intended body while
  its reference vertex indices remain ambiguous. Give those facts separate
  response fields and program branches. When a measured geometric model admits
  finitely many correspondences or rigid symmetries, retain the supported set
  and propagate it to the next action predicate. A unique index assignment is
  unnecessary if every supported hypothesis gives the same relevant envelope
  or passes that predicate with its stated uncertainty. Reject hypotheses with
  actual contradictory measurements; do not select one merely to pass a gate.
  If supported hypotheses disagree on the effect, obtain relevant information
  or use another justified bounded action. Same-body identity alone establishes
  neither a complete transform nor retained attachment.
- Check future observation dependencies before an occluding intervention. A
  local motion witness can establish retention without establishing its relation
  to a later shape envelope. Acquire the needed relation while observable, or
  implement a later witness or symmetry-invariant construction that does not
  need unavailable named features. Explain which distinction a proposed view
  action can resolve. Repeating an unchanged self-occluded view, or asking for
  the same missing index assignment under a new name, is not new information.
- Treat goal-pose tolerance and actual effect uncertainty separately. After a
  bounded pose lease, evaluate the relevant measured geometry before declaring
  an object-level outcome. A small residual is neither failure nor proof of the
  object effect. Do not double-count a future control allowance as an unobserved
  current displacement after the actual geometry has been measured. Heuristic
  uncertainty is not a calibrated multi-sigma certificate.
- Checkpoint acknowledged jaw transitions and phase intent before a later
  observation can fail. A repair must distinguish approach, possible holding,
  measured retention, and actual release. After release, a missing observation
  alone is not a reason to regrasp or disturb the object; seek bounded additional
  evidence or report uncertainty. Model proposals and native task scores differ.

- A valid reference patch can become untrackable after viewpoint or occlusion
  changes. An unknown registration is not proof of a lost object. Design a
  bounded current-observation fallback for each phase that uses registration,
  rather than only at initialization. Semantically defined, visually identifiable
  corresponding landmarks can provide independent motion evidence when their
  uncertainty and identity checks are adequate. If they are not adequate, seek
  another justified observation or stop. Never turn a command prediction into a
  measured object transform. Store the reference definitions and measurements
  before motion so a later fallback or repair can use their actual provenance.
- Check exact numerical-helper return fields before using them. In particular,
  a plane fit returns coefficients, not an undocumented alias for that vector.
  Early interface mistakes consume the same limited repair budget needed for
  genuinely new physical observations. An offline-valid source still requires
  real execution and native evaluation.

- Check that finite phase loops can cover the remaining work under the smallest
  progress leg actually used, including visibility fallbacks. Reducing a leg
  length without updating the route bound can make completion impossible even
  when every local action succeeds. View changes consume calls but are not
  necessarily target-directed progress. Reserve calls for later phases; a
  coherent budget is not a collision or convergence certificate.

- Scope prerequisites to the action being considered. Certifying an entire later
  transfer route is not a prerequisite for every earlier noncontact observation
  or approach. Each phase needs its own attainable evidence and bounded fallback.
- The runtime does not certify collision-free swept volumes. Distinguish visible
  obstruction, incomplete visibility, and certified clearance. Do not invent the
  third capability or make it an implicit mandatory sensor.
- If a needed view is missing, consider a bounded observation-producing action
  justified by the current local evidence, or return a specific capability gap.
  Repeatedly reviewing an unchanged occluded scene cannot create a new view.
- The robot's measured finger geometry and proprioception can support reasoning
  about its own envelope. They do not prove object contact or retained load.
  Ask visual reviews for the missing object evidence, not for information already
  available numerically about the robot.
- Match measurement requests to the published review capacity. Use supported
  named point/region fields; arbitrary metadata is not an executable sensor.
- Prefer a concise complete method with useful local checks and recovery over
  a long list of redundant global gates. None of these lessons proves that the
  next generated method will complete the task; actual execution is required.
- Report the numerical values behind a failed geometric check in trace notes or
  result evidence. Arbitrary fixed object-size ranges are not physical laws.
  Derive grasp clearances and margins jointly from measured object dimensions,
  own finger geometry, measurement uncertainty, and controller tolerance. A valid
  small object can make independently chosen fixed margins mutually infeasible.
- A depth sample at a visual boundary can hit an adjacent surface. Check
  consistency with an interior measured surface rather than assuming all marked
  corners have equally reliable depth. Current calibration and a fitted plane
  support explicitly derived ray intersections for genuinely visible planar
  landmarks, with the plane-fit uncertainty and correspondence limits retained.
- Jev never sees a question's dictionary ID. Identical axis question text with
  identical criteria does not identify six different axes. Specify each subject
  and feature selector in question content. The control compiler now binds the
  axis selector explicitly; arbitrary branch questions still need self-contained
  instructions. Two real zero-motion comparisons supported this fix on one
  stored state; they are not task-success or general direction-accuracy results.
- Camera-relative corner names are not persistent physical identities. Supply
  semantic landmark definitions and reference observations/geometry to subsequent
  reviews, or implement uncertainty-aware correspondence from available data.
  A changed view must not silently redefine which physical point an ID denotes.
  Historical projections assume stationarity and must not be treated as current
  object measurements after manipulation.
- Closure can hide the outline while leaving a textured interior patch visible.
  Requiring a complete perimeter before a justified retention-measurement lift
  can create another circular precondition. The RGB-D registration primitive
  was checked on synthetic translations/outliers and on recorded pregrasp/closure
  views with partial occlusion. That is measurement evidence, not a completed
  physical task or a universal tracking guarantee; unknown still needs recovery.
- Initialize a reliable textured reference before a motion that occludes it when
  possible. A camera suitable for an object's geometric outline need not be the
  best camera for texture registration. Keep each ROI tied to its own camera and
  observation frame; inspect feature-count errors and choose a better visible
  interior patch rather than blindly repeating the same inadequate selection.
- Use exact response field names from the current manual and actual receipts.
  A descriptive phrase such as current observation does not imply an additional
  current_frame_id key: the tracker uses frame_id and reference_frame_id. Include
  relevant measured values in evidence before a later operation can fail; a
  method repair starts a fresh Python namespace while physical effects persist.
- A gate labelled clear can silently require complete visibility even when the
  requested fact was only absence of a visible external obstruction. Ask for
  separate obstruction and visibility evidence with defined decision meanings.
  Repeated observation moves that preserve the same self-occlusion do not resolve
  that uncertainty. Use a justified local action or a genuinely different view;
  never replace unknown with certified clearance. Preserve valid historical
  geometry explicitly instead of rebuilding every unrelated prerequisite after
  a repair. These lessons do not authorize motion through an observed obstacle.


# Program runtime v2: exact API

The host owns the LIBERO OSC_POSE environment. Images are current 768x768 RGB,
top-left pixel origin. Depth and calibration support metric backprojection.
Robot state is proprioception and own finger geometry only. World units are m,
rotation vectors rad, quaternions xyzw. Nothing exposes hidden object state.

Available globals: np, math and geo; define main(api). The exact allowed builtins are
abs, all, any, bool, dict, enumerate, float, int, len, list, max, min, range,
reversed, round, set, sorted, str, sum, tuple, zip, isinstance, type, Exception,
RuntimeError, ValueError and RPC-backed print. Other builtin names are unavailable;
for example, use Exception rather than an undeclared exception class.
The complete source limit is 120000 ASCII characters; all helpers must resolve.
Return completion_proposed as a boolean and evidence as a JSON-compatible object
or list. A list of diagnostic log entries is supported by the repair interface.
On repair, previous_method.incomplete_result.program_result contains the actual
program-returned outcome with its own field names preserved. It is program
evidence, not native evaluator feedback. A top-level evidence log longer than
12 entries retains its latest 12 with explicit evidence_excerpt counts. Other
feedback lists are bounded to 40 entries and strings to 6000 characters; dense
world point clouds are summarized. Full original outcomes remain in raw records.
Treat excerpts and historical measurements according to their scope and provenance.
All API arguments/results are JSON-compatible: use ndarray.tolist() at boundaries.
print(...) and api.note(text) write bounded trace notes through host RPC.
Structured data numbers sent to GPT/Jev use six significant digits; tool schema
constraints remain exact so a declared numeric enum or bound is not changed.
The worker's API data, numerical control and original execution receipts retain
full precision. Calculate geometry using API measurements rather than assuming
displayed decimal length establishes sensing accuracy.

## Pure numerical helpers

geo contains pure numerical helpers, not robot skills or task policies. Its
arrays are local NumPy arrays; use .tolist() for API arguments. No helper reads
sensors, chooses a measurement region, controls motion or accepts a task goal.
Use these instead of generating equivalent formulas:

- geo.rotation(quaternion_xyzw): active 3x3 tool-to-world matrix; unit quaternion.
- geo.transform(points, matrix): N x 3 points transformed by a proper rigid 4x4.
- geo.pad_position(state): world pad center from api.state() and own tool offset.
- geo.plane(points): >=3 noncollinear 3D points. Returns coefficients [nx,ny,nz,d]
  with normal toward +z, center_world_m, rms_m and two in_plane_spread_m values.
- geo.circle_xy(points): >=3 noncollinear XY or XYZ samples. Returns center_xy_m,
  radius_m, rms_m, max_radial_error_m, largest_angular_gap_rad. This fits XY only;
  check horizontal-plane evidence and boundary identity separately.
- geo.attachment_error(points_before, points_after, state_before, state_after):
  maximum world discrepancy in m between corresponding measured points and the
  motion predicted by the measured TCP rigid transform. Does not label a grasp.

Fits reject malformed/nonfinite/degenerate inputs but do not certify model
adequacy. The program chooses correspondences, uncertainty, thresholds and
recovery. Return meaningful diagnostic values when a fit is rejected.

## Observation and geometry

- api.state(): frame_id, native_steps, budgets, tcp_position_world_m,
  tcp_quaternion_xyzw, gripper_qpos_m, last_gripper_command, own_geometry.
  own_geometry contains pad_center_in_tool_m, pad_extent_in_tool_m,
  finger_low_offset_tool_m and finger_high_offset_tool_m.
- api.point(camera, pixel, radius=3): current visible surface point as
  world_m, depth_m, frame_id, pixel, camera, source. camera is agentview or robot0_eye_in_hand.
  pixel=[u,v]; radius 1..6. Invalid/discontinuous depth raises an error.
- api.camera(camera): current K, camera_to_world_opencv, frame_id.
- api.plane_point(camera, pixel, plane): intersect the calibrated current pixel ray
  with a program-supplied world plane [nx,ny,nz,d], n dot X + d = 0. Returns
  world_m, pixel, plane, frame_id and an explicit derived-source label. Rejects
  grazing, behind-camera and out-of-range intersections. Fit/validate the plane
  from actual visible measurements first. This can support visible boundary
  landmarks whose depth patch mixes surfaces; it does not prove that a selected
  pixel belongs to that plane or reveal a hidden object boundary.
- api.cloud(camera, box, stride=6): sampled visible surface points world_m,
  corresponding rgb and pixels, frame_id, camera, box, stride, source.
  box=[u0,v0,u1,v1], integer image bounds.
  stride 4..32. Includes background/occluders; no object isolation is implied.
  Process it yourself; geometric extrema need validity checks.
- api.compose(quaternion_xyzw, rotation_delta_world_rad): compose a world
  rotation-vector delta with a quaternion; returns quaternion xyzw.
- api.track_init(camera, polygon): initialize a generic textured RGB-D surface
  patch tracker on a currently visible 3..16 vertex polygon. Returns handle,
  reference_features and frame_id; at least 12 textured depth-valid features are
  required. Up to 32 handles per physical episode. Handles persist across source
  repairs in that same episode; a new episode starts with an empty tracker bank.
  The receipt also identifies camera, method_number and source_sha256 at creation.
  Save a useful handle, its physical identity, camera/ROI and reference frame in
  a checkpoint if a repair may need it. Restoring a handle is not a fresh pose:
  call track_update for current evidence and reject unknown or inadequate quality.
  Reuse only a reference to the same physical surface; do not repurpose a handle
  for a new object merely because its identifier is available.
- api.track_update(handle): compare the reference patch with both current views
  using SIFT descriptors, depth backprojection and robust rigid registration.
  Returns status tracked or unknown. tracked includes a 4x4
  transform_initial_world_to_current_world, camera, frame_id (current observation),
  reference_frame_id (initial observation; there is no current_frame_id field),
  matches, inliers, rms_m, inlier_spread_m, uncertainty_floor_m, and reference/current
  inlier world points (reference_inlier_world_m, current_inlier_world_m) and patch
  centroids (reference_patch_centroid_world_m, current_patch_centroid_world_m).
  Apply the rigid transform to a point
  to obtain its position: its translation column alone is not point displacement
  when rotation is present. unknown provides no pose estimate. No physics advances.
  This tracks a caller-selected textured surface, not a named object oracle.
  Validate identity, rigidity, feature coverage and uncertainty before using it.
  Partial occlusion may still leave enough correspondences; total occlusion or
  insufficient texture yields unknown. unknown returns frame_id, reference_frame_id,
  reason, candidates and source, but no transform or pose estimate. A transform alone does not certify a grasp.
  Comparing observed patch motion with measured hand motion can support retention
  tests without requiring every object perimeter corner to remain visible.
  The current tracker can retain up to eight appearance keyframes, always keeping
  the initial one. At least six physical steps must separate additions. Growth
  requires at least 12 registration inliers, fraction >=0.65 and RMS <=0.0015 m.
  Up to 200 new features are accepted only where inverse registration projects
  into the original eroded polygon with original-depth agreement <0.0025 m.
  New feature coordinates remain in the initial world reference. The initial
  patch centroid and reference_frame_id do not change. A propagated heuristic
  uncertainty floor accompanies derived features; this is not a calibrated
  confidence bound. No appearance growth occurs after unknown registration.
  tracked additionally returns appearance_reference with keyframes, features,
  added_features, last_keyframe_frame_id and support. These describe historical
  appearance support, not a new object-identity or grasp sensor. Incorrect initial
  identity or an incorrect accepted registration can still cause tracking drift.
  Feature extraction uses a spatial budget: a 4x4 image grid, up to 128 features
  per cell (2048 total), rather than discarding weak local texture against one
  global strongest-feature quota. tracked returns feature_search with raw_features,
  selected_features, grid and per_cell_limit; candidates contain per-view counts.
  This improves measurement coverage but does not establish object identity or
  guarantee visibility. unknown still provides no extrapolated pose.
- api.review(question, context=None, fields=None): obtains fresh images and a real GPT observation review.
  Declare fields for branch-critical parameters. It is a dict of parameter names
  to type descriptors: "boolean", "number", "integer", "string"; a list of
  string enum literals; or a small JSON Schema object. The host sends these as
  an actual strict function-tool object, not JSON encoded inside a free string,
  and validates exact returned types without coercion. For example, a declared
  boolean cannot become the string "yes", and an enum literal cannot become true.
  All declared fields are required, with no undeclared properties. Nested object
  descriptors use type/object/properties; nested arrays use type/array/items.
  Strings default to maxLength6000, arrays to maxItems64; optional values can use
  type:["boolean","null"] (or another type plus null). Supported constraints:
  enum, description, minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, minItems/maxItems.
  No refs, patterns, anyOf, arbitrary extra properties or implicit defaults.
  At most32 top-level fields, depth8,256 nodes and16384 ASCII declaration chars.
  Property names are ASCII identifiers of at most64 characters.
  Return parameters is still a dict. Data-shape validation is not evidence truth.
  Use explicit unknown enum/null values where missing evidence needs distinction.
  Ask for the exact declared names/types and validate geometry separately.
  New and repaired methods must supply fields for every review. fields=None is
  available only to untouched archived methods for backward compatibility.
  Each review supports at most 32 named points and 8 named regions. Request only
  the measurements needed now; use additional reviews when a valid view is missing.
  Returns status (continue/complete/stop), explanation, parameters (dict),
  points (dict name -> api.point result), regions (dict name -> api.cloud result),
  measurement_errors (list of {name,error}), frame_id. A requested point/region
  whose measurement fails is omitted from its dictionary and listed in
  measurement_errors. Inspect membership and errors before indexing: a selected
  pixel is not a successful depth sample. Fit only sufficient valid measurements;
  otherwise obtain a bounded replacement observation or report the exact gap.
  The program receives only this call's measurements. Historical observations
  shown to the reviewer are context and are not automatically merged into its
  return. Save valid partial measurements before retrying or repairing; reuse
  needs justified identity/freshness, not merely the same requested name.
  Specify the needed visible evidence and named measurements explicitly.
  Parameters are a model interpretation, not independent sensor certification.
  Named region requests have explicit camera, box and stride fields; stride is
  4..32. Arbitrary region_strides inside parameters are not executable requests.
  Review sees previous review images, your question, current state, and receipts.
  It does not read your source or invent a new API. Every review uses GPT budget.
  Optional context is your JSON-compatible reference geometry, label definitions,
  or other needed program state. Historical initial/previous label annotations
  are also retained within the current method execution, together with current
  camera projections of previous world points under a stationary-point hypothesis.
  These projections are reference aids, not tracking detections or current poses.
  Physical landmark IDs must persist across camera motion; screen upper-left is
  not a stable identity. Reference annotation scope resets for a repaired method.

## Real Jev and bounded physical action

api.control(target, quaternion, gripper, questions, features=None,
            tool_point="tcp", translation_limit=0.02, rotation_limit=0.10,
            steps=3, position_tolerance=0.006, rotation_tolerance=0.06)

target is a desired world point. quaternion is the desired tool orientation xyzw.
tool_point is tcp or pad_center (host subtracts the rotated own pad offset).
gripper is open/close/keep. This requirement is sent to Jev; the actual gripper
choice is dispatched unchanged. Features is your JSON-compatible processed state.
The host adds trusted current robot state, pose residuals, and axis relations.
Each translation/rotation vector is L2-limited; translation_limit 0.001..0.02,
rotation_limit 0.01..0.10. A decision executes 1..3 native steps. A goal farther
than 0.6m is rejected. No object collision certification or grasp is implicit.
position_tolerance accepts 0.0005..0.012 m; rotation_tolerance 0.01..0.10 rad.
Tighter tolerances do not certify physical accuracy or successful convergence;
they can require more decisions, and every controller still has bounded budgets.

questions is a dictionary with exactly x,y,z,rx,ry,rz,gripper. Each value is:
{"type":"choice","instructions":"...","criteria":{"option":"meaning",...}}.
The six axis keys have exactly negative,hold,positive; gripper has open,close,keep.
You author instructions and criteria. The host maps negative/hold/positive to
-1/0/+1, times bounded magnitudes derived from absolute pose residuals. Positive
means increasing world coordinate or positive world rotation-vector component.
Host axis relation is increase/decrease/within_tolerance. The host does not fix
Jev's answer. Inputs include controller limits and a source-labelled feature dict.

Exact wire state: {"robot": <state()>, "processed_features": {"program": <your
features>, "objective": {"gripper": ..., "tool_point": ...},
"translation_error_world_m": [...], "rotation_error_world_rad": [...],
"axes": {"x": {"error": ..., "goal_relation": ...}, ...}}, "feature_source": ...}.
The compiler prefixes each control question with its explicit
state.processed_features.axes.<axis>.goal_relation selector (and the objective
gripper selector), then appends your instructions and preserves your criteria.
Question names alone are labels, not sufficient semantic bindings. Full compiled
requests and unchanged answers are archived. No answer is silently corrected.
Jev does not see the question ID at all: each question is evaluated from its
instructions/criteria against state. Therefore all custom api.choose questions
must state their subject and relevant feature fields explicitly as well.
Source: https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice (request structure).
The numerical controller uses a per-axis deadband of the respective pose
tolerance divided by sqrt(3): magnitude is zero inside it, including when Jev
selects a nonzero sign. Outside it the signed bounded residual rule applies.
This is declared magnitude computation, not a substituted Jev direction.

Returns status (reached/moved/stalled), choices, before, after, target_tcp,
position_error_m, rotation_error_rad, native_steps, acknowledged_steps, frame_id.
before, after and target_tcp are each a length-3 world TCP position list in m,
not state dictionaries and not pad positions. Use api.state() for full states.
reached uses measured post-action pose and commanded-gripper delivery only.
It does not prove any object effect. status=stalled means negligible translation
despite a nontrivial translation residual; verify your objective before retrying.

api.drive(target, quaternion, gripper, questions, features=None, max_calls=30,
          **controller_limits)
is an optional generic local feedback lease using exactly the same control
interface. Each update still calls real Jev with current robot residuals and
dispatches its answer unchanged. It stops on reached, three consecutive stalled
updates, or max_calls (integer 1..40). Returns the last receipt and lease_calls;
status is reached, stalled, or lease_exhausted.
The returned before/after describe only the last control update, not the whole
lease. Save api.state() before the lease if measuring whole-lease progress.
It does not choose task phases, verify object effects, retry a grasp, or perform
recovery. Program-authored
features remain fixed within this lease; use individual control calls if those
features must be recomputed each update. All normal episode budgets still apply.

api.choose(questions, features): real Jev choices for finite local branch decisions.
Each question uses the same type/instructions/criteria shape. At most 8 questions,
2..8 options each. Returns choices and frame_id. It executes zero robot steps.
Never treat it as an image observation: Jev receives structured text features.

## Persistence, failure and budgets

- api.checkpoint(key, value): retain caller-owned JSON data across method repairs
  in this physical episode. key is 1..64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dots
  or hyphens. At most 16 keys, 16384 bytes per value and 131072 total value bytes.
  Overwriting a key is allowed. Returns key, frame_id, method_number,
  source_sha256, bytes and source. The host adds these provenance fields; it does
  not certify the content. Store only useful measurements, assumptions,
  uncertainties, landmark identities and acknowledged phase evidence.
- api.recall(key=None): without a key, return a list of checkpoint metadata;
  with a key, return that record plus value. Unknown keys raise an error. The
  planner sees the metadata manifest, not every value automatically. Memory is
  empty in a new episode and is never loaded from an archived method. Stored data
  are historical program assertions, not fresh observations or native success.
  Revalidate identity, stationarity and dependencies before reuse. Tracker handles
  and Python objects are not preserved by storing their names in JSON.

Every physical control request invokes Jev and every native step has a receipt.
State and measurements change only after actual motion. Scene geometry can become
stale after any motion. Python in one submitted method persists until return;
a repaired method starts a fresh Python namespace in the same physical scene.
No reset exists. All loops must be finite. Invalid calls raise RuntimeError.
The host enforces total GPT/Jev/native-step/wall budgets across repairs and reviews.
Stop with an incomplete result if needed evidence or resources are unavailable.
